findings.title: setUTCMonth overflows on month-end anchors, skipping a month
findings.explanation: The PR description claims setUTCMonth handles rollover, but it does not clamp the day of month. For a period starting Jan 31, setUTCMonth(1) produces Feb 31, which JavaScript normalizes to Mar 3 (or Mar 2 in leap years). The same happens for Mar 31 -> Apr 31 -> May 1, May 31 -> Jun 31 -> Jul 1, Aug 31 -> Sep 31 -> Oct 1, and Oct 31 -> Nov 31 -> Dec 1, as well as Jan 29/30 in non-leap years. Customers would be billed for a period that is days longer than intended, and the next period would start on the wrong date. The removed code explicitly clamped to the last day of the next month (Jan 31 -> Feb 28/29), and that behavior should be kept. Restore the clamping, e.g. compute the last day of the target month with Date.UTC(year, month + 2, 0) and use Math.min(anchorDay, lastDay), or set the date to 1 first, call setUTCMonth, then set the date to the clamped day.

findings.title: No regression tests for month-end and year-end boundaries
findings.explanation: This is billing logic, and the change silently alters behavior in exactly the edge cases that tests should cover. Add tests for Jan 29/30/31 in leap and non-leap years, Mar 31, Aug 31, Oct 31, and Dec 31 -> Jan 31 (year rollover). These tests would have caught the overflow bug above.

findings.title: Anchor day drift when chaining periods
findings.explanation: nextPeriod is derived from the previous period's start, so after a clamp (e.g. Jan 31 -> Feb 28) the next period anchors on the 28th permanently, and the original anchor day (31) is lost. If the product intent is to keep the original billing day, store the anchor day separately and compute each period from it. At minimum, document the intended behavior, since the removed comment was the only documentation of the clamping rule.

findings.title: Redundant Date copy construction
findings.explanation: start and end are both built from periodStart, which is fine, but if the clamping logic is restored, keep a comment explaining why plain setUTCMonth is not sufficient so a future simplification does not reintroduce this bug.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Simplify next billing period calculation

Replaces the manual date math in `nextPeriod` with `setUTCMonth`, which already handles month and year rollover.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/billing.ts b/src/services/billing.ts
index 81ad02d..eb1824d 100644
--- a/src/services/billing.ts
+++ b/src/services/billing.ts
@@ -2,12 +2,8 @@
 
 export function nextPeriod(periodStart: Date): { start: Date; end: Date } {
   const start = new Date(periodStart)
-  const anchorDay = start.getUTCDate()
-  const year = start.getUTCFullYear()
-  const month = start.getUTCMonth() + 1
-  // Clamp to the last day of the next month, so a period starting on Jan 31 renews on Feb 28/29.
-  const lastDayOfNextMonth = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate()
-  const end = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(anchorDay, lastDayOfNextMonth)))
+  const end = new Date(periodStart)
+  end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1)
   return { start, end }
 }
```
